messages:
Alex Choi: Quick question — when someone saves a query from a route page (Route Insights), should the default scope be the current route or the org/team? cc @Maria
Maria Gomez: my vote is default to route. 99% of saves from route page are route-specific. avoid surprising users by making it global.
Sahil Patel: +1 for route default, but we need to think about quotas and telemetry. if every team saves the same route-filtered query we could blow up saved-query counts and telemetry joins.
Jun Li: what about a lightweight explicit option in the save modal: radio buttons "Visible to route / Visible to team / Personal"? default selected = route. keeps UX clear.
Emily Park: agree with Jun. also we should persist a `scope` field in the API so it's unambiguous (route/team/personal) and a `scope_id` when applicable. avoids ad-hoc bool flags.
Alex Choi: that helps. API sketch:```json
{
  "name": "high-cost-400ms-filter",
  "query": "model:fast-llama AND latency_ms>400",
  "scope": "route",
  "scope_id": "route_0a1b2c",
  "created_by": "alex.c"
}
```
Maria Gomez: nice. note: UI should surface current scope on saved-queries list and the route page should prefer showing route-scoped queries first.
Sahil Patel: about telemetry: we still want to attribute which saved queries are used in A/B rollouts. we need a cheap join key emitted in logs when a saved query is applied: `saved_query_id`. sampling must preserve that field.
Jun Li: +1. also add server-side dedupe when saving: if another team already saved an identical route-scoped query, suggest linking instead of creating duplicate. reduces clutter.
Emily Park: migration question — existing saved queries have no scope. do we default them to org? route? I think route where last_used_from_route_id exists, otherwise org.
Alex Choi: that migration heuristic sounds fine. just document it and don't change visibility silently. notify owners during rollout.
Sahil Patel: one more: console permissions — route-scoped queries should respect route-level RBAC (who can view that route). i.e., don't show route-scoped saved queries to folks without access.
Maria Gomez: agreed. UX note: add small badge "route" or "team" and a tooltip explaining visibility.
Emily Park: plan for rollout: behind FF `saved_query_scope_by_default`, default on in beta console for 2 weeks, then enable for all. also emit a migration job with dry-run logs.
Jun Li: I'll prototype the modal copy and wire up API contract. Alex, can you add a short acceptance criteria doc for PM review?
Alex Choi: on it. I'll add ACs (what counts as identical query, migration rules, telemetry fields).
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: feature-flag:saved_query_scope_by_default -> canary(10%) at 2025-03-15T09:12:00Z
Maria Gomez: sweet — thanks all. we should also update docs and the tutorial that shows saving from a route.
Sahil Patel: fine to close once prototype + FF + migration dry-run logs look good.
Alex Choi: thanks team, moving to follow-up doc in product/pm.
